blocks.arabic_text: قَدْ سَمِعَ قَوْلَ قَوْمِكَ لَكَ، وَأَنَا مَلَكُ الْجِبَالِ، وَقَدْ بَعَثَنِي رَبُّكَ إِلَيْكَ لِتَأْمُرَنِيْ بِأَمْرِكَ،فَمَا شِئْتَ، (إِنْ شِئْتَ۞) أَطْبَقْتُ عَلَيْهِمُ اْلاَخْشَبَيْنِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: بَلْ أَرْجُو أَنْ يُخْرِجَ اللهُ تَعَالَي مِنْ أَصْلَابِهِمْ مَنْ يَعْبُدُ اللهَ وَحْدَهُ، لَا يُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئاً.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه مسلم، باب ما لقي النبي ﷺ من اذي المشركين والمنافقين، رقم:٤٦٥٣
blocks.tamil_translation: “O Rasulullah, have you faced a day harder than the day of Uhud?” asked Hazrat Aishah (RA). Rasulullah ﷺ said, “I suffered great hardship from your people. On the day of Aqabah (in Ta'if) I had to suffer the most. When I put my request before Ibn Abd Yalil ibn Abd Kulal (the chief of the people of Ta'if), “Bring Iman in me, be a help to me, and help me by giving me a place to stay so that I can do the work of Da'wat freely,” he did not listen to what I said. I began walking (back) on my way (away from Ta'if) with great grief and sorrow. When I reached the place called “Qarn-ath-Tha'alib', (my grief and sorrow) eased a little. At that moment I saw a piece of cloud above my head giving me shade, and when I looked closely I saw Hazrat Jibra'il (AS) in it. He called me and said, “Allah Ta'ala has heard the words your people spoke to you and their reply. He has sent the angel in charge of the mountains to you; command him with whatever you wish.” After that the angel appointed over the mountains called me, greeted me with Salam, and said, “O Muhammad! (ﷺ) Allah Ta'ala has heard the words your people spoke to you. I am the angel in charge of the mountains. Your Lord has sent me to you, telling me to carry out whatever you wish to command me.
